claim: A warrantless inspection of sealed cargo containers by port authority officers constitutes an unreasonable search under the Fourth Amendment absent exigent circumstances or a recognized administrative exception. The court held that the commercial nature of the premises does not categorically diminish the owner's reasonable expectation of privacy in locked freight.
citation: Yeldham v. Consolidated Port Authority of New Jersey, 847 F.2d 319 (3d Cir. 1988)
initial_reasoning: Yeldham v. Consolidated Port Authority of New Jersey held that warrantless inspections of sealed cargo containers by port authority officers were not unreasonable under the Fourth Amendment because the commercial nature of the premises and the lack of a reasonable expectation of privacy in locked freight justified the search. This directly contradicts the claim that such inspections constitute an unreasonable search absent exigent circumstances or a recognized administrative exception.
